# SepFormer official parity fixtures

`official-fp64/` contains one independent oracle for each of the seven public
SpeechBrain SepFormer checkpoints supported by Vokra. The fixtures were
generated with the pinned official `speechbrain==1.0.3` model, at the exact
upstream revisions recorded in each `manifest.json`, by:

```text
uv run --project tools/parity --locked python \
  tools/parity/sepformer_dump_reference.py ... --dtype float64
```

The model and input execute in float64. Arrays are then serialized as
little-endian f32 so Rust can embed them without a new runtime dependency. The
dumper never imports Vokra, reads a GGUF, or falls back to a local mirror of the
network. `SHA256SUMS` pins every generated byte.

## Numerical boundaries

The encoder and the WSJ02Mix, Libri2Mix, Libri3Mix, WHAM16k, WHAMR16k, and
WHAMR-8kHz waveforms retain the established `max_abs <= 0.01` and
`mean_abs <= 0.001` boundaries.

DNS4 is separately gated at `max_abs <= 0.1513` and
`mean_abs <= 0.00515`. This is not a blanket relaxation. The pinned official
SpeechBrain FP32 waveform itself is ill-conditioned after the first dual-path
block:

- the same official FP32 reference generated on Apple ARM and VAST x86 differed
  by max `0.0972996`, mean `0.00243752`;
- Apple official FP32 versus official FP64 differed by max `0.0399671`, mean
  `0.000860898`;
- VAST official FP32 versus official FP64 differed by max `0.0756435`, mean
  `0.00257070`.

The DNS4 boundary is twice the largest observed official FP32-to-FP64 floor,
rounded upward (`2 * 0.0756435 = 0.151287`,
`2 * 0.00257070 = 0.0051414`). On the Apple validation run, Vokra CPU versus
the FP64 oracle measured max `0.08839798`, mean `0.00243860`; Metal measured
max `0.11425972`, mean `0.00306709`; and CPU versus Metal measured max
`0.06386566`, mean `0.00141754`. The subsequent VAST x86 CPU run at commit
`f02a7556` measured max `0.12589264`, mean `0.00357618` against the same FP64
fixture, also inside the pre-registered DNS4 boundary.

DNS4 selects the portable scalar reduction order only for its CPU path. The
other six variants retain normal CPU ISA dispatch. Metal remains fully
GPU-dispatched and never silently falls back to CPU.
